summary: Geo failover caused token-bucket drift and sustained soft 429s for multi-region dedicated pool
description: Issue summary: After an automated geo-failover triggered during a regional maintenance window, TellusSearch began receiving an elevated rate of 429 responses (soft throttles) from our multi-region Dedicated pool. Impact: ~10% of streaming sessions from TellusSearch were receiving intermittent 429s; customer reports degraded UX and elevated error rates in US-east users. Timeline: 2026-03-10 03:05 UTC - scheduled route drain in eu-west; 2026-03-10 03:12 UTC - automated failover completed; 2026-03-10 03:15 UTC - TellusSearch alerts and ticket opened. Expected behaviour: failover should preserve token-bucket state and not cause sustained soft throttles. Observed behaviour: sustained elevated 429 rate for ~90 minutes localized to requests routed from eu-west into us-east serving pool. This appears correlated to token-bucket counters and lease timestamps not reconciling post-failover.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use a dedicated API key attached to a multi-region customer pool (TellusSearch setup). 2) Initiate geo-drain or failover on eu-west while active streaming clients remain connected. 3) Observe 429 spike within 5-10s and elevated soft-429 rate for subsequent 30-120 minutes as token-bucket balances do not re-sync between region proxies.
logs_and_metrics: 429 rate increased from baseline 0.2% to 6.4% for TellusSearch between 2026-03-10T03:12Z and 2026-03-10T04:45Z. Error signature: 'rate_limit_exceeded: token_bucket_drift' seen in api-gateway logs. Sample trace ids: trace-122334-03, trace-122334-11. Token-bucket counter snapshots: us-east proxy reported remaining_tokens=0 at 2026-03-10T03:13Z while eu-west proxy reported remaining_tokens=5200 and a last_reset_ts earlier than us-east, resulting in double-debit protection kicking in on requests routed to us-east. CPU/memory on serving nodes normal; scheduler logs show rapid host reassignments during the drain window.
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: token-bucket lease timestamps are not synchronized across region-edge proxies during failover, which allows tokens to be counted separately and then reconciled causing negative balance on target proxy. Verified: edge-proxy metrics show mismatch in last_reset_ts across regions up to 120s. Checked NTP skew: host clocks within 50ms. Checked pubsub event reorder: observed out-of-order route update event processed by us-east proxy ~3s after eu-west, but reconciliation logic expects eventual consistency and has a race. Looked at scheduler: host reassignment triggered immediate re-route without waiting for token-bucket state delta propagation. Related PR modifying fast-route-rollout path merged 2026-03-08 (runtime PR #4521) may have reduced reconciliation window. Hypothesis: new fast-rollout path reduced token-bucket reconciliation window causing temporary negative effective tokens on the receiving proxy, leading to soft throttles instead of graceful fallback.
customer_communication: 03/10 03:20 UTC - Sent initial acknowledgement and mitigation plan to TellusSearch (M. Alvarez). We explained we were investigating a failover-related throttle spike and provided guidance to temporarily stagger client reconnects. 03/10 05:10 UTC - Follow-up with ETA for mitigation (config rollback + hotfix) and recommended a safe retry/backoff pattern in their uploader. Customer requested postmortem and prevention plan.

next_steps: 1) Apply hotfix to routing service to force immediate token-bucket reconciliation on cross-region route transfers (PR referenced). 2) Add integration test for geo-failover token-bucket handoff. 3) Backfill monitoring: create a dashboard alert for region-to-region token_reset_ts delta > 50s. 4) Share postmortem with TellusSearch and update runbook for scheduled maintenance to include safe reattach window. 5) Consider rate-limit behavior change to prefer graceful degraded throughput rather than immediate soft-429 during reconciliation.
resolution: In progress - temporary rollback applied for affected customer allocation and per-customer mitigation recommended. Hotfix development in progress; aiming for deployment 2026-03-13. Pending postmortem and runbook updates.
